Subject: MSA security exhibit - prioritization & evidence cadence (HealthSync)

Jordan —

Thanks for taking this on. We just finished an internal review and have three priority asks on the security exhibit and audit language before procurement can move to signature:

1) Pen test notice & window: we need a firm 60-day notice for production pen tests, and a preferred window (no earlier than Mar 1, 2027) to align with our release calendar.
2) Audit rights: carveouts for multi-tenant customer data + a preferred timeline for SOC 2 evidence requests (we expect quarterly requests during onboarding then ad hoc).
3) Evidence cadence: HealthSync security team needs an evidence matrix showing ownership (Redwood artifact, Redacted sample, or customer-run test) and an ops contact for each artifact.

I attached our redline pass (HealthSync_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx) and a starter evidence matrix (healthsync-evidence-matrix.xlsx). Can your legal and security teams triage and propose a prioritized list of items we can close in the next two weeks? Procurement needs a short runway to lock pricing.

If helpful, Michael and I are available next week for a 30-minute triage call — suggested times in the attachment.

Best,

Emma / Jordan —

Thanks — Laura here from Legal. I read HealthSync_MSA_Redlines_v3 and the evidence matrix. Below are the concrete items we can action and the ones that need negotiation: 

A) Pen test notice / window (P0) — Proposed language: 
""
Provider will provide Customer with written notice of any planned penetration test against Customer-dedicated resources at least sixty (60) days prior to the planned test date. Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to accommodate mutually agreeable test windows; Provider may require a non-production (staging) window for tests that could impact production stability.
""
This preserves a 60-day notice while giving Redwood operational recourse to suggest staging. If HealthSync requires a hard production-only window on a particular date, that would need a separate SOW/ops carveout.

B) Audit rights / multi-tenant carveout (P1) — We cannot grant unfettered on-site access to multi-tenant infrastructure. Proposed compromise: a scoped audit right limited to (i) Provider-controlled logs and tracings relevant to Customer’s instance, (ii) SOC 2 report access and attestations, and (iii) redacted sample artifacts for configuration proofs. On-site privileged inspection would be allowed only with 90-days’ notice and executed under a defined inspection protocol (ephemeral access, scoped accounts, NDA addendum).

C) Evidence cadence (P2) — Operations can supply a populated matrix. For recurring SOC 2 evidence requests, suggest: initial onboarding packet within 7 business days of contract execution; quarterly health-check evidence snapshots (summary artifacts) thereafter; ad-hoc requests handled with 10 business days’ SLA unless request requires log extraction or forensics.

D) Items requiring commercial approval from Sales (Jordan / Ben): any timeline extension that would shift Go-Live or require committed engineering hours (e.g., custom audit extracts).

I’ve attached a redline excerpt with the clause snippets and a short rationale (see attachment: HealthSync_MSA_Redlines_v3-docu-redline.txt). Please review; I will push a tracked-change version to the DocuSign link once we confirm language.

Happy to join the alignment call suggested. Tuesday 22 Dec 10:00 PT works for me.

—Laura Bennett
